cli.name: help
cli.output:
Irresponsible Rust IRIX Simulator

Usage: iris [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --config <CONFIG>
          Path to iris.toml config file [default: iris.toml]
          
          [default: iris.toml]

      --prom <PROM>
          Path to PROM image

      --machine <NAME>
          The machine to emulate: a `[machine] profile` name such as `octane_ip30`. Overrides the config file. `--machine help` lists them

      --nvram <NVRAM>
          Path to NVRAM file (default: nvram.bin in cwd)

      --nveeprom <NVEEPROM>
          Path to Indigo2 motherboard EEPROM file (default: nveeprom.bin in cwd)

      --bank0 <BANK0>
          RAM bank 0 size in MB (0/8/16/32/64/128; IP28 also supports 256/512)

      --bank1 <BANK1>
          RAM bank 1 size in MB (0/8/16/32/64/128; IP28 also supports 256/512)

      --bank2 <BANK2>
          RAM bank 2 size in MB (0/8/16/32/64/128; IP28 also supports 256/512)

      --bank3 <BANK3>
          RAM bank 3 size in MB (0/8/16/32/64/128; IP28 also supports 256/512)

      --jitv2-threads <N>
          jitv2 compile-pool thread count (fixed at startup, see jitv2.threads)

      --scsi1 <SCSI1>
          SCSI ID 1 image path (HDD)

      --scsi2 <SCSI2>
          SCSI ID 2 image path (HDD)

      --scsi3 <SCSI3>
          SCSI ID 3 image path (HDD)

      --cdrom4 <CDROM4>
          SCSI ID 4 image path (CD-ROM, primary disc)

      --cdrom5 <CDROM5>
          SCSI ID 5 image path (CD-ROM, primary disc)

      --cdrom6 <CDROM6>
          SCSI ID 6 image path (CD-ROM, primary disc)

      --scsi7 <SCSI7>
          SCSI ID 7 image path (HDD)

      --no-write-cache
          Report every hard disk's write cache off (`write_cache = false` in each `[scsi.N]`): every write is stored on the host's disk before the guest is told it is done, as on the drives SGI shipped. Slower. The default is a write cache, which can lose about 5 s of writes in a host crash (see STORAGE.md)

      --cdrom4-extra <ISO>
          Additional ISO images for CD-ROM ID 4 (can be specified multiple times)

      --cdrom5-extra <ISO>
          Additional ISO images for CD-ROM ID 5 (can be specified multiple times)

      --cdrom6-extra <ISO>
          Additional ISO images for CD-ROM ID 6 (can be specified multiple times)

      --2x
          2× window scaling for HiDPI/4K monitors

      --headless
          Run headless: no window, no REX3 graphics (audio unaffected; use --noaudio to disable)

      --noaudio
          Disable audio emulation (no HAL2); graphics still works

      --audio-host <HOST>
          Host audio system for HAL2: default, alsa or pulseaudio (overrides [audio] host)

          Possible values:
          - default:    The platform's usual one: CoreAudio on macOS, WASAPI on Windows, ALSA on Linux
          - alsa:       ALSA (Linux)
          - pulseaudio: A PulseAudio server, or PipeWire's pipewire-pulse (Linux). Falls back to ALSA when none answers

      --nfs-dir <DIR>
          Enable NFS share: path to the directory to export (enables NFS)

      --nat-subnet <CIDR>
          NAT subnet in CIDR notation (e.g. 192.168.5.0/24). Gateway gets .1, guest (IRIX) gets .2. Default: 192.168.0.0/24

      --net-mode <MODE>
          Networking backend: "nat" (default, software gateway) or "pcap" (bridge onto a real host interface; requires --features pcap)

          Possible values:
          - nat:    Built-in software NAT gateway (ARP/DHCP/DNS/ICMP/TCP/UDP + port forwarding). Works without any host privileges or extra libraries. This is the default
          - pcap:   Bridge raw Ethernet frames onto a real host interface via libpcap (Linux/macOS) or a WinPcap-compatible driver (WinPcap or Npcap) on Windows. Requires building with `--features pcap` and elevated privileges at runtime. The guest appears as a real L2 host on the physical LAN; NAT services (DHCP/DNS/NFS/port-forward) are NOT provided — use the real network's
          - off:    No Ethernet: the adapter is not plugged into anything. O2 and Octane only (`MachineConfig::validate`); the Indy and Indigo2 always have a network
          - stream: A private segment carried over a stream socket in QEMU's `-netdev stream` framing, to a peer that serves it (`[network] stream`). iris provides no gateway services on it

      --pcap-interface <IFACE>
          Host interface to bridge onto in PCAP mode (e.g. eth0, en0). Implies --net-mode pcap. List candidates with --list-net-interfaces

      --validate
          Check the configuration (`--config`, with any other options applied) without starting the machine: that it parses, that its settings agree, that its files and directories exist and its ports differ. Exits 0 if it would run, 1 with each problem on stderr if not

      --list-net-interfaces
          Print the host network interfaces libpcap can bridge onto, then exit. Requires a build with --features pcap

      --no-scsi-deferred-int
          Disable deferred SCSI status interrupts (default: enabled for OpenBSD/NetBSD compatibility)

      --cpu <MODEL>
          Emulated CPU: `r4400` (default), `r5000`, or `r10000`. Overrides `[machine] cpu`.
          
          All three models are compiled into every build — each is its own monomorphisation, so the hot path carries no per-model branch — and this picks between them at construction. The `r5k` Cargo feature is removed.

          Possible values:
          - r4400:  MIPS R4400, 16K direct-mapped L1s, 1 MB L2. The Indy IRIS has always shipped
          - r5000:  MIPS R5000, 2-way 32K L1s, no secondary cache, MIPS IV
          - r10000: MIPS R10000, 2-way 32K L1s, 1 MB secondary cache, MIPS IV. The CPU in the Indigo2 IMPACT (IP28). The machine uses shadow cache arrays; see `docs/indigo2-ip28.md` and `src/cpu/mips_cache_shadow.rs`

      --cache <MODEL>
          Cache model: `auto` (default: `shadow` in a jitv2 build, else `full`), `full` or `shadow`. Overrides `[machine] cache`. The R10000 is always `shadow`
          
          [possible values: auto, full, shadow]

      --graphics <BOARD>
          Graphics board: `newport` (default), `xz`, `extreme`, `solidimpact`, `highimpact`, `maximpact` (or `impact:solid`, `impact:high`, `impact:max`)

          Possible values:
          - newport:     Newport (REX3) — fully emulated. Default
          - xz:          GR2 XZ (2 GE7) — Indy XZ or Indigo2 XZ (`src/dev/gr2`). In bring-up
          - extreme:     GR2 Extreme (8 GE7) — Indigo2 only (`src/dev/gr2`). In bring-up
          - solidimpact: Solid IMPACT (1 GE11, 1 RE4)
          - highimpact:  High IMPACT (2 GE11, 1 RE4)
          - maximpact:   Maximum IMPACT (2 GE11, 2 RE4)
          - v6:          VPro V6: BUZZ A, 32 MB. Octane only (`src/dev/odyssey`)
          - v8:          VPro V8: BUZZ A, 128 MB. Octane only
          - v10:         VPro V10: BUZZ B, 32 MB. Octane only. It shipped only in the Octane2 and needs Crossbow 1.4, so the machine takes the Octane2's Crossbow and Bridge revisions
          - v12:         VPro V12: BUZZ B, 128 MB. Octane only. It shipped only in the Octane2 and needs Crossbow 1.4, so the machine takes the Octane2's Crossbow and Bridge revisions
          - none:        No graphics board: the machine runs on its serial console. Octane only
          
          [aliases: --board, --graphics-board]

      --gdb-port <PORT>
          Enable GDB stub on the given TCP port (e.g. --gdb-port 1234). Connect with: target remote localhost:<port>

      --monitor-port <PORT>
          Monitor console port on 127.0.0.1 (default 8888). Give each iris running at once its own

      --vnc [<ADDR>]
          Serve the screen, keyboard and mouse over VNC on ADDR (`host:port`, or a port on 127.0.0.1; default 127.0.0.1:5900). Works with a window, with --ci, and on every graphics board

      --serial-port-a <PORT>
          Serial channel A (tty2) port on 127.0.0.1 (default 8880)

      --serial-port-b <PORT>
          Serial channel B (tty1, the console) port on 127.0.0.1 (default 8881)

      --serial-socket-a <PATH>
          Also serve serial channel A on this Unix socket

      --serial-socket-b <PATH>
          Also serve serial channel B on this Unix socket

      --keyboard <LAYOUT>
          Physical host keyboard: `ansi` (default), `iso` or `jis`. Use `jis` for a Japanese keyboard with the PROM's `keybd` set to JP

          Possible values:
          - ansi: US-style: `\|` above Enter
          - iso:  European ISO: extra key left of Z, `#~`-style key left of Enter
          - jis:  Japanese JIS 106/109: `]}` left of Enter, plus `¥`, `ろ` and the conversion keys

      --test-device
          Map the bare-metal test device into GIO expansion slot 0: SIGNATURE, PUTC (guest console → stdout), DUMP (machine state → JSON) and EXIT (terminate with the guest's exit code). Off by default

      --test-device-dump <FILE>
          Where the test device writes its machine-state dump

      --cheritest-dump-hook
          cheritest convention: a guest write to CP0 register 26 dumps machine state. Needs --test-device. Never enable for a normal boot — CP0 26 is ECC on a real R4400 and the PROM writes it during cache init

      --tftp-dir <DIR>
          Serve this directory read-only over TFTP at the gateway address, so the PROM can network-boot from it: `boot -f bootp()<file>`. Off when unset

      --rsh-dir <DIR>
          Let the guest `rsh <gateway> cat|ls|echo|pwd` against this directory, read-only, through a built-in rsh server at the gateway (TCP 514). Nothing is executed on the host. Off when unset

      --load-elf <FILE>
          Load a static ELF32 MSB (big-endian MIPS) binary into RAM before the CPU starts and set PC to its entry point, instead of booting the PROM. For bare-metal test binaries; see also the monitor's `loadelf`

      --perfetto <FILE>
          Record a Perfetto trace into FILE from startup (build with `--features perfetto`). Open it at ui.perfetto.dev

      --perfetto-cats <LIST>
          Perfetto categories, e.g. `irq,gfx` or `all,-jit` [default: all]

      --perfetto-clock <CLOCK>
          Perfetto timeline: `host` (ns) or `guest` (instructions) [default: host]

      --ci
          CI mode: enable the control socket and apply speed-favoring fidelity shortcuts. Hides the window unless --ci-display is set; offscreen graphics remain active unless --headless is explicitly set

      --ci-socket <PATH>
          Override the default control-socket path (iris.sock in $TMPDIR, else /tmp)

      --ci-display
          With --ci, keep the Newport window visible for interactive test development (deferred rendering at 10–15 fps)

      --serial-log <FILE>
          With --ci, append every byte the guest emits on ttyd1 (IRIX serial console) to this file. Useful for live tailing during an install

      --serial-log-timestamps <MODE>
          `off` (raw transcript) or `wall`: prefix each completed serial-log line with a UTC ISO-8601 timestamp

          Possible values:
          - off:  Raw bytes, byte-for-byte a transcript (the default)
          - wall: `[YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ] ` before each completed line
          - ecs:  One ECS JSON line per completed, non-empty line (logger `irix.guest`)

      --serial-log-a <FILE>
          Write what the guest sends on serial channel A to this file when A is not the console (Indy, Indigo2)

      --serial-log-b <FILE>
          Write what the guest sends on serial channel B to this file when B is not the console (Octane, O2)

      --clock-fixed-mhz <MHZ>
          Override CP0 Count MHz (default 33 on IP22/IP24, 97.5 on IP28). IRIX reports twice this rate as CPU MHz, e.g. --clock-fixed-mhz 50

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
